data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: buy
sections.question: buy
sections.summary: to get something by paying money for it

senses.definition: to get something by paying money for it
examples: She went to the shop to buy some milk and bread.
He bought a new jacket at the department store on Saturday.

answers.answer: She went to the supermarket to buy food for the whole week.
He went to the library to buy a new book for his daughter.
She tried to buy some fresh air at the park near her house.
He used his card to buy the table at the restaurant for the meal.

sections.title: cashier
sections.question: cashier
sections.summary: a person whose job is to take payments from customers in a shop or bank

senses.definition: a person whose job is to receive and pay out money in a shop, bank, or hotel
examples: She paid for her shopping at the cashier near the exit.
The cashier gave her the wrong change, so she asked for a receipt.

answers.answer: She paid for her shopping at the cashier near the exit of the supermarket.
He asked the cashier to fix his broken laptop at the shopping centre.
She went to the cashier to get a new passport for her holiday abroad.
He asked the cashier to cook his dinner and bring it to his table.

sections.title: credit card
sections.question: credit card
sections.summary: a small plastic card that lets you buy things and pay for them later

senses.definition: a small plastic card that allows you to buy things and pay for them later
examples: She used her credit card to pay for the new television online.
He always pays by credit card when he shops online.

answers.answer: She used her credit card to pay for the new sofa at the furniture shop.
He showed his credit card to the police officer to prove his identity.
She ate her sandwich with her credit card because she forgot a fork.
He planted his credit card in the garden to grow more money for the future.

sections.title: discount
sections.question: discount
sections.summary: a reduction in the usual price of something

senses.definition: a reduction in the usual price of something
examples: She got a ten percent discount because she had a student card.
The shop gave a big discount on all winter coats in January.

answers.answer: She got a twenty percent discount on the jacket because she had a student card.
He asked for a discount at the restaurant to make his food taste hotter.
She applied a discount to her hair to make it look shiny and clean.
He wore a discount badge on his shirt to show he worked at the store.

sections.title: mall
sections.question: mall
sections.summary: a large building containing many shops, restaurants, and other businesses

senses.definition: a large enclosed building containing many shops, restaurants, cafés, and other businesses
examples: She spent the whole afternoon at the mall buying clothes and shoes.
The new mall in the city centre has over a hundred shops inside.

answers.answer: She spent the whole afternoon at the mall looking for a new pair of shoes.
He went to the mall to swim twenty lengths before breakfast.
She cooked Sunday dinner at the mall for the whole family.
He slept at the mall every night because it was close to his work.

sections.title: money
sections.question: money
sections.summary: coins and banknotes used to buy things; the total amount you have to spend

senses.definition: coins and banknotes used to pay for things; the amount you have available to spend
examples: She saved enough money to buy a new bicycle for her birthday.
He didn't have enough money to pay for the meal.

answers.answer: She saved her money for three months to buy a new laptop.
He drank all his money at the café and had nothing left to eat.
She wore all her money to the party because she wanted to look rich.
He ate his money quickly at the restaurant because he was very hungry.

sections.title: price
sections.question: price
sections.summary: the amount of money you need to pay to buy something

senses.definition: the amount of money that you must pay in order to buy something
examples: The price of the jacket was fifty pounds, which was too expensive for her.
She always checks the price before buying anything online.

answers.answer: She checked the price of the shoes before deciding to buy them.
He ate the price of his meal at the restaurant without any complaint.
She wore the price tag on her new coat because she liked how it looked.
He cooked the price at home every week to try to save more money.

sections.title: receipt
sections.question: receipt
sections.summary: a piece of paper that shows you have paid for something

senses.definition: a piece of paper that proves you have received goods or paid for something
examples: She kept the receipt in case she wanted to return the shoes later.
He asked the cashier for a receipt after paying for his shopping.

answers.answer: She kept the receipt so she could return the jacket if it did not fit.
He drank the receipt to show the waiter that he had already paid for the meal.
She cooked the receipt in the oven to make it easier to read.
He planted the receipt in his garden because the paper was very good quality.

sections.title: sale
sections.question: sale
sections.summary: a time when a shop sells goods at reduced prices

senses.definition: a period when a shop sells goods at reduced prices
examples: She bought three new dresses during the summer sale.
The January sale is the best time to buy a new television.
The sale of the house took three months to complete.

answers.answer: She waited for the January sale to buy a new coat at a lower price.
He drank a big glass of cold sale after his morning run in the park.
She added a pinch of sale to the soup to give it a better flavour.
He planted sale in his garden to grow flowers for the spring.

sections.title: sell
sections.question: sell
sections.summary: to give something to someone in exchange for money

senses.definition: to give something to someone else in exchange for money
examples: She decided to sell her old bicycle because she had bought a new one.
He sells handmade cards at the market every Saturday morning.

answers.answer: He sells handmade cards at the market every Saturday morning.
She went to the bakery to sell a fresh loaf of bread for her lunch.
He tried to sell the rain to the farmers so their crops would grow.
She tried to sell her homework to her teacher at the end of the lesson.

sections.title: supermarket
sections.question: supermarket
sections.summary: a large shop that sells food, drink, and household goods

senses.definition: a large shop that sells food, drink, and household products
examples: She goes to the supermarket every Saturday to buy food for the week.
The new supermarket near our house is open until midnight.

answers.answer: She goes to the supermarket every Saturday to buy food for the week.
He went to the supermarket to see the doctor about his sore throat.
She studied for her exam at the supermarket because it was very quiet.
He swam thirty laps in the supermarket before doing his weekly shopping.
